$comment: CS193V managed Claude Code policy. Lives at /etc/claude-code/ — deliberately NOT
under ~/.claude, which is a named volume: an image-provided file there would be
seeded once on first mount and never refreshed by a later image. In /etc it is part
of the image layer, so every --rebuild and every image update restores it.
What is deliberately ABSENT, and why:
defaultMode          - Claude Code's own default is kept. Permission prompts are
how a student learns what the agent wants to do, which is
the core skill of the course. Since the container is the
boundary, loosening it buys convenience, not safety.
autoUpdatesChannel   - auto-update stays ENABLED, so students always have current
Claude Code. Measured rather than assumed (issue #13): the CLI
is installed as the student, its updater detects an npm-global
install, and its update path runs `npm install -g` with no
--prefix -- so it rewrites the student's own prefix in place,
no sudo needed. Two accepted costs: versions drift between
students, and each update copies ~283 MB into the container's
writable layer (overlayfs copies a modified file up in full),
which every --rebuild discards and the next update re-fetches.
requiredMinimumVersion / requiredMaximumVersion - NEVER add these. They cause a
hard startup exit, which combined with a pinned image can
manufacture a container that refuses to start at all.
MCP configuration    - none shipped, and not locked down either.
The deny rules below stop ACCIDENTS, not attacks, and must be described that way.
An agent with Bash can read any of these files with `cat` regardless; no permission
rule can prevent that. What they do prevent is the ordinary case: an agent globbing
the home directory while looking for config, pulling a live token into its context,
where it can end up in a saved session transcript.
Scope is deliberate and asymmetric. ~/.config/gh and the Vercel directory are denied
WHOLESALE, because the agent has no legitimate reason to look in either and the
credential filenames may change between tool versions. ~/.claude is denied only at
the credential FILE, because that directory also holds settings.json, plans/ and
session transcripts that the agent may legitimately need when a student asks why
their own configuration behaves a certain way.
Only Read(...) and Edit(...) forms are used. Write(...) and Glob(...) path rules are
accepted by Claude Code and then SILENTLY IGNORED with a startup warning — a
security control that does nothing is worse than none. See VERIFICATION.md A.3
(deny-rule-forms) and A.11, which assert this both statically and functionally.
